topic: At breakfast Femi's seven-year-old asked him which of his pub friends would survive longest in a zombie apocalypse. Femi has just admitted to the table that he said Hugh would last longest and Danny would go first.

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: First? I've survived the M50 in fog, Femi.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: Fog's not a zombie, Danny. You'd stop to argue with the first one about its tone.

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: Why would I last longest? I'd just shut the yard gate
T.full: Why would I last longest? I'd just shut the yard gate and carry on. They'd be no worse than the walkers.

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: That gate's hanging off, Hugh!

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: So that's Hugh out, then.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: No, no, Hugh'd get bitten on the Tuesday, say nothing, and by Friday Will's dragging him in going Dad's a funny colour and he's growling at the dog.

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: How would anyone

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: I'd bite you first, Danny.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: See, that's exactly what I told him. Hugh doesn't need to survive, he just becomes management.

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: Hang on, where'd I come, then? I've got a van full of copper pipe and a blowtorch
T.full: Hang on, where'd I come, then? I've got a van full of copper pipe and a blowtorch, I'm not going out before a solicitor.

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: You'd be in a reservoir somewhere.

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: Zombies can't swim, Jess!

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: Course they can, they're dead, Rhiannon. Dead things float. You'd have forty of them bobbing after you down the Wye going, wait, wait.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: They sink first, Danny
T.full: They sink first, Danny. Then float.

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: Why do you know that? Why'd you know that so fast, Sunny?

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: I grew up by the cut, bab.

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: She's right, mind. Lost a ewe in the Lugg in '07, never saw her again till she come up by Leominster, fortnight after.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: Hang on, how'd you know it was her, though?
T.full: Hang on, how'd you know it was her, though? A fortnight in the Lugg, I wouldn't recognise my own mum.

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: Ear tag, Femi. Still in, and all. She'd always had her eye on Leominster, that one.

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: Nobody has their eye on Leominster, Hugh. I've had chips there, she'd have turned round and swum back.

backchannels.after: Nobody has their eye on Leominster, Hugh.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: Go on, what'd you give it?

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: Four. Four, and that's only 'cause she called me love
T.full: Four. Four, and that's only 'cause she called me love and chucked extra scraps on. Batter was grey, Femi. Grey.

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: That's Pauline. Calls everyone love.

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: Pauline! God, you should see her loft.

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: Every story in this town ends up in someone's loft with you. Go on then, what was it? Tell me it was bodies.

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: No, worse than bodies. Went up for her tank, right, and it's, it's wall to wall Take a Break, bundled in string, going back to like ninety-four, and every puzzle done. In pen
T.full: No, worse than bodies. Went up for her tank, right, and it's, it's wall to wall Take a Break, bundled in string, going back to like ninety-four, and every puzzle done. In pen. Every single one, Danny, and she's down the ladder going mind my wordsearches.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: In pen? Since ninety-four? Femi, rip your list up, Pauline's seeing us all out, that woman's never once needed a rubber.

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: Pen's just showing off, that.

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: That's why Derek left, that.

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: Derek did not leave over puzzles, Hugh, Derek left with Shelley off the Spar till
T.full: Derek did not leave over puzzles, Hugh, Derek left with Shelley off the Spar till, the whole town knows that.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: Shelley with the nails? Never!

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: Who are any of these people?

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: You don't know Shelley? Femi. You've been here, what, five years, and you don't, she did both my girls' nails for their leavers' do.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: Tobi'd know her. He's seven and the lad on the Co-op till already holds the reduced doughnuts
T.full: Tobi'd know her. He's seven and the lad on the Co-op till already holds the reduced doughnuts back for him.

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: He's got a dealer, Femi.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: Ours was worse, bab. Dev at eight was selling his nan's Bombay mix out his book bag, fifty pence a bag, and the head rings me at surgery going—
